compilers.paper_statement: clang/LLVM (v4.0), and GCC (v7.0) compilers built from recent (August 2016) upstream development sources

time_anchor.fact: Clang 3.9.0 final was tagged 2016-08-31 from the 3.9 branch at r280312 and announced 2016-09-02. That release includes -flto=thin. The release notes, last updated 2016-08-31, still say ThinLTO is new and point at the June blog.
time_anchor.compatible_with_paper: A v4.0 development compiler in August 2016 can already have -flto=thin. That does not identify one commit.

compilers.future_pin_rule: Only a paper, a contemporaneous author artifact, an explicit benchmark or build record, or another verifiable historical build may become a reconstructed pin. A commit chosen because the date is close is not a pin.

rejected_pins.why: A release tag. The paper says August 2016 upstream development sources, not the 4.0.0 release.
A later release. The paper's v7.0 is the August 2016 development line, not a release tarball.
The 3.9 release, not the paper's v4.0 development sources. It shows -flto=thin already existed. It is not the compiler under test.

build_performance.paper_string: 16 core (32 logical) 2.9GHz Intel Xeon CPU ES-2690 with 64GB memory, running Linux and using the gold linker

runtime_spec.runs: five runs, discard highest and lowest, average the remaining three

external_spellings_not_corrections.role: A later slide spells the build machine differently. It does not edit the paper.

section_8_2.scale_corroborated_without_a_revision: November 2016 author slides show 1,938 Clang IR files and 217 MB at -g0, the same scale as the paper, and still name no checkout
The same slides show 17,798 Chromium IR files and 706 MB at -g0. No DEPS revision or gn args are attached.

section_8_2.paper: An internal Google datacenter application that serves targeted ads.

section_8_4.note: Bazel distributed build of the private application. Not part of a public matrix.

8.2_link_scaling.llvm_lto_parallelism: LLVM LTO optimizes in a single thread, and only the codegen is parallel

figure_text_conflicts.where: Section 8.2 prose versus the LLVM Developers' Meeting 2016-11 slides
figure_text_conflicts.resolution: none. The paper token stays ES-2690.

memory_metric.paper: peak difference between the resident set size and the shared memory as reported by the Linux kernel
memory_metric.rationale: Shared memory accounts for read-only mmapped files that the kernel keeps in RAM. That memory is inside RSS but is not treated as pressure.
memory_metric.note: A later runner that records only peak RSS is a different measurement, not a reproduction of this metric.

paper_defined.paper: changes the implementation of a frequently referenced function in a widely used header, forcing many files to rebuild
changes the implementation of an infrequently called function in an implementation file

external_candidates_not_the_paper_worklo.build_machine: 20-core 2.8GHz Intel Xeon CPU E5-2680 v2, Linux, gold, ninja clang
external_candidates_not_the_paper_worklo.not_section_8_3: Published before the paper's August 2016 sources, on a different machine from the 16-core ES-2690 host. Related earlier experiment, not the CGO section 8.3 run.
external_candidates_not_the_paper_worklo.if_used_later: Directional operationalization only. Not an Exact paper workload.

thinlto_backend_cache.key: input IR file hash combined with the thin-link analysis results
thinlto_backend_cache.hit: backend loads the cached native object

extra_compiler_caches.why: They are not the cache Section 3 describes. Turning them on, or turning the ThinLTO backend cache off, measures a different build.

accept_as_reconstructed_pin: an explicit benchmark or build artifact
search_stop_rule.reject: a commit or checkout selected because its date is close

must_resolve_before_exact_matrix.why: Exact section 8.2 and 8.3 claims need the checkout that produced the paper's build graph.
Exact section 8.2 claims need the checkout behind the published link size.

must_resolve_before_exact_matrix.item: build flags that define the experiment
must_resolve_before_exact_matrix.status: partially locked from the paper; -O2 versus -O3 remains a conflict
must_resolve_before_exact_matrix.why: An exact matrix cannot pick a side of that conflict.

may_operationalize_before_directional_ma.rule: A later public checkout may be recorded only as pin_class operationalization, with supports_exact false. It is not a reconstructed pin. None is recorded now, because no build log or revision string selects one.

paper_unspecified.item: gold, binutils, CMake, and Ninja versions
paper_unspecified.paper: names gold, and does not name these versions

not_pins.why: A later switch, default off, described as starting to evaluate ThinLTO. It cites the June blog, not this paper, and does not identify the checkout behind section 8.2.
